disclaimer: Fictional example robot for demonstration. Not based on any real customer project. Every result requires review by a qualified functional-safety engineer.

robot.name: CS-1 Concierge Robot (fictional)
robot.definitionRef: ISO 13482:2014, 3.14 (mobile servant robot: travels to perform serving tasks in interaction with humans, e.g. exchanging information)
robot.intendedUse: Autonomous information and wayfinding robot in indoor public buildings (airport terminals, shopping malls, hotel lobbies). Answers questions on a touchscreen and by voice, and escorts visitors to a destination at walking pace.

parameters.sensors: Front and rear safety laser scanners (IEC 61496-3 Type 3), downward ToF cliff sensors, perimeter bumper (PSPE), 3D camera (non-safety, navigation only)
parameters.humanInterface: 21-inch touchscreen, microphone/speaker, status light ring, emergency stop button on the rear upper body
parameters.connectivity: Wi-Fi fleet management (remote send-to-goal and pause commands)

robot.environment: Indoor, flat hard floors and carpet, ramps up to 5 %, crowds at peak hours, escalators, moving walkways and stairs in the building.
robot.users: General public including children, elderly persons, wheelchair users and persons with visual or hearing impairment (untrained). Venue staff (trained operators). Service technicians.

small.reason: 1.3 m tall: a falling robot can hit the upper body of a child or a seated person (6.1.2.1 NOTE 1).

lightweight.reason: 70 kg: a trapped person cannot reliably lift it, and impact can cause more than minor injury (NOTE 2).

slow.reason: 1.0 m/s (60 m/min) is not slow for the intended user group: elderly visitors walk slower than this, and NOTE 3 ties 'slow' to the intended user group's walking speed as determined by risk assessment.

noManipulator.reason: No arm; touchscreen and head only.

robotTypeClassification.rule: Type 1.1 requires small AND lightweight AND slow AND no manipulator; any 'no' gives Type 1.2.

plrMethod.primary: ISO 13482:2014 Table 1 (Tables 3-9) value for Type 1.2, per 6.1.3. Deviations only via 6.1.4 with documented risk assessment.
plrMethod.crossCheck: ISO 13849-1:2023 Annex A risk graph (Figure A.1), P from Table A.1/A.2. Used to test whether 6.1.4 could demand a different PL, and to derive PLr for functions not listed in 6.1.1 a)-g).
plrMethod.precedence: ISO 13482 Table 1 > manual/6.1.4 deviation > risk graph.

hazards.title: Collision with a person during autonomous travel or guiding
hazards.hazardousSituation: Robot travels at up to 1.0 m/s through a crowded terminal; a person steps into its path or approaches from the side (4.2 d).
hazards.harm: Impact, knock-down and fall; for elderly persons hip fracture or head injury.
hazards.inherentlySafeDesign: Rounded shape and soft outer cover (5.10.8.2 c); maximum speed limited by drive design.
hazards.informationForUse: Describe collision avoidance behaviour (5.10.8.4); light ring and sound to make the robot noticeable (5.14).

hazards.title: Contact with a person the scanner cannot detect (small child, person on the floor) or during close interaction at the screen
hazards.hazardousSituation: A small child runs below or very close to the scanner plane, or a visitor stands against the robot while it starts to turn or move off.
hazards.harm: Child knocked over; foot run over by a wheel; trapping between robot and wall.
hazards.inherentlySafeDesign: Bumper and lower body without pinch points; wheels shrouded (5.6, 5.13).

hazards.title: Robot falls down stairs or off a floor edge
hazards.hazardousSituation: Localization error or map change brings the robot to a staircase, mezzanine edge or open floor hatch.
hazards.harm: Robot (70 kg) falls onto persons below or on the stairs.
hazards.inherentlySafeDesign: Restricted space defined away from stairs where possible (5.16.2 a).
hazards.informationForUse: Specify environments and conditions where localization errors can occur (5.16.4).

hazards.title: Robot enters a forbidden area (escalator or moving-walkway landing)
hazards.hazardousSituation: While escorting a visitor, a navigation or localization error leads the robot onto an escalator landing.
hazards.harm: Robot falls or is carried onto the escalator; persons on the escalator crushed or knocked down.
hazards.inherentlySafeDesign: Escalator zones excluded from all routes in the map (5.12.2 a).
hazards.informationForUse: Installation instructions for floor markers and forbidden-zone setup.

hazards.title: Unexpected start-up, restart or remote command
hazards.hazardousSituation: Robot is powered on or receives a fleet 'send-to-goal' command while a visitor is standing next to it; Wi-Fi link drops mid-task.
hazards.inherentlySafeDesign: Start-up self-test of safety functions; start in restricted speed (5.4.2 a, c).

hazards.title: Any situation needing an immediate manual stop
hazards.hazardousSituation: Staff or visitor sees a person trapped or the robot behaving abnormally.
hazards.note: Touchscreen and voice cannot serve as an emergency stop; a physical button on the robot gives the equal level of safety (6.2.2.2).

otherHazardsCovered.item: Overturning onto a person (leaning, ramp turn, collision)
otherHazardsCovered.measure: Inherent design: low centre of gravity, wide support area, stability tested; no stability control used for risk reduction, so 6.1.1 g) does not apply (5.10.2.2).

otherHazardsCovered.item: Sharp edges, gaps, shape during collision

otherHazardsCovered.measure: Sound and light ring (5.14); not an SRP/CS function.

otherHazardsCovered.item: EMI causing loss of safety function

otherHazardsCovered.measure: Safety functions SF3-SF7 do not depend on the AI/navigation stack (5.12, 5.16.2 b).

safetyFunctions.name: Emergency stop
safetyFunctions.trigger: Emergency stop button on the robot body is pressed.
safetyFunctions.reaction: Stop category 0 or 1 (IEC 60204-1) of all motion; drive power removed; latched.
safetyFunctions.safeState: Robot stopped, drives de-energized, brakes applied.
safetyFunctions.reset: Manual only; reset does not restart the robot (6.2.2.2 f).

riskGraphCrossCheck.note: Emergency demand is rare; trapped person cannot escape.

safetyFunctions.name: Protective stop with monitored standstill
safetyFunctions.trigger: Demand from SF3, SF5, SF6, SF7; failed start-up self-test; loss of fleet/command connection during motion; power-on.
safetyFunctions.reaction: Stop category 1 or 2 with standstill monitoring; unintended motion during standstill gives category 0 stop.
safetyFunctions.reset: Automatic restart only after the person has left the protective stop space (5.14.3 c), otherwise manual. Power-on always ends in monitored standstill until a user action (5.4.3 b).

riskGraphCrossCheck.note: For H5: unexpected motion next to an unaware visitor.

openQuestions: Is automatic restart acceptable in all public areas, or only outside designated child areas?

safetyFunctions.name: Hazardous collision avoidance (safety laser scanner, speed-dependent fields)
safetyFunctions.trigger: Person detected in the protective stop space; field size switched with actual speed.
safetyFunctions.reaction: Warning field: request speed reduction (SF4). Protective field: protective stop (SF2).
safetyFunctions.safeState: Robot stopped before reaching the person.
safetyFunctions.designNotes: Minimum distance per ISO 13855 (6.5.2.1), braking distance under worst floor condition (6.2.3); detected relative approach speed may replace K.

riskGraphCrossCheck.note: Raw risk graph gives e. ISO 13849-1:2023 A.2 allows a one-level downgrade if probability of occurrence is justified as low (most persons notice the robot and step aside, 5.14 measures) -> d, consistent with Table 7. Engineer decision: A.2 downgrade accepted, PLr d (no 6.1.4 deviation).

safetyFunctions.name: Safety-related speed control
safetyFunctions.trigger: Always active. Limit switched by context: 1.0 m/s normal; 0.5 m/s when a person is in the warning field, after start-up, near the dock and on ramps.
safetyFunctions.reaction: Speed above active limit or speed-monitoring fault gives a protective stop.
safetyFunctions.safeState: Speed at or below active limit, or robot stopped.
safetyFunctions.designNotes: Limits from speeds of representative points (6.4); only authorized persons can change limits.

riskGraphCrossCheck.note: Same exposure as SF3; same A.2 downgrade argument applies. Engineer decision: A.2 downgrade accepted, PLr d (no 6.1.4 deviation).

safetyFunctions.name: Safety-related force control (perimeter bumper)
safetyFunctions.trigger: Bumper (PSPE) actuated anywhere around the base.
safetyFunctions.reaction: Protective stop and short reverse to release the person.
safetyFunctions.designNotes: Low actuation force and coverage at child foot/leg height (5.10.8.3 NOTE 3). Force reaction per 6.7 a)-b).

riskGraphCrossCheck.note: Starting point after SF4 (0.5 m/s near persons) and soft bumper (A.2: additional safety functions are taken into account). Table 9 value d is higher and governs. Engineer decision: S1 confirmed.

safetyFunctions.name: Forbidden area avoidance (escalators, moving walkways)
safetyFunctions.trigger: Robot position (from localization) reaches a virtual forbidden-zone boundary, OR a floor marker at an escalator approach is detected, OR localization confidence drops below threshold.
safetyFunctions.reaction: Protective stop before the boundary; motion out of the zone only at safety-related reduced speed (6.3).
safetyFunctions.safeState: Robot stopped outside the forbidden area.
safetyFunctions.designNotes: Two diverse sensing principles (map localization + floor markers) per 5.12.3 d); markers placed without blind spots (6.5.3); restricted space bounded by actual stopping position (6.3).

riskGraphCrossCheck.note: Escalator approaches passed occasionally; persons on escalator cannot escape.

safetyFunctions.name: Drop-off detection (travel surface sensing for stairs and edges)
safetyFunctions.trigger: Downward ToF sensors detect a floor drop beyond the step-height limit ahead of the robot.
safetyFunctions.reaction: Protective stop within the sensing distance at current speed.
safetyFunctions.designNotes: Independent of navigation (5.16.2 b). Braking distance on worst floor checked (6.2.3).

plrTypeC.source: ISO 13482:2014, Table 1 row 'Limits to workspace (incl. forbidden area avoidance 6.5.3)', Type 1.2 (mapping confirmed by engineer)

riskGraphCrossCheck.note: Stairs only in a few locations; persons below cannot avoid a falling robot.

standardsHint.note: Functional safety scope only. US mapping to be verified by the engineer in the Standards Map step.

reviewLog.decision: Keep PLr d per ISO 13482 Table 6/7; A.2 one-level downgrade accepted, no 6.1.4 deviation to PL e.
S1 confirmed (starting point after SF4 reduced speed and soft bumper); PLr d per Table 9.
Travel surface sensing (6.5.3) mapped to the Table 1 row 'Limits to workspace (incl. forbidden area avoidance)'; PLr d.
'slow' = no: 1.0 m/s is not below the walking speed of elderly users. Type 1.2 unchanged.
